findings.message: CPU peaked at 91.4% — server is CPU-saturated. Response times will degrade under further load.
Error rate at 5.72% — exceeds acceptable threshold. Check server logs for connection timeouts or application exceptions.
Transaction 'T-US01_Overall_Iteration' is 4.26x slower than average (2522ms vs 592ms). Priority optimization target.
Azure App Service returned 168 5xx errors during the test window. Server-side failures detected.

ai_insights.executive_summary: The 60-second load test executed 10,881 samples at 182 req/s, but only 3.4% of transactions met SLA targets (1 of 29). Average response time was 592 ms with P99 at 4,489 ms, and error rate reached 5.72% (exceeding 1% target). Server CPU peaked at 91.4%, indicating saturation, and 168 HTTP 5xx errors were recorded.

data_quality_findings.issue: Test duration limited to 60 seconds; may not capture steady-state behavior or garbage collection cycles.
data_quality_findings.evidence: Test duration reported as 60 seconds with no ramp-up/down details.
data_quality_findings.impact: Confidence in sustained performance characteristics is reduced; saturation effects may be underrepresented.
data_quality_findings.action: Extend test duration to 15-30 minutes with gradual ramp-up to observe steady-state metrics.

data_quality_findings.issue: Concurrency level (virtual users) not explicitly reported; throughput and response time used to infer load.
data_quality_findings.evidence: Total samples and throughput provided, but no virtual user count or thread group configuration.
data_quality_findings.impact: Capacity planning estimates rely on Little's Law approximations rather than controlled concurrency.
data_quality_findings.action: Capture and report active virtual user count per interval in future tests.

data_quality_findings.issue: Database and JVM telemetry absent; cannot isolate application-tier vs data-tier bottlenecks.
data_quality_findings.evidence: Only Azure App Service CPU/memory/network/disk metrics provided; no SQL metrics, GC logs, or thread dumps.
data_quality_findings.impact: Root cause analysis limited to infrastructure saturation; database contention or lock contention cannot be ruled out.
data_quality_findings.action: Enable Azure SQL monitoring, JVM GC logging, and application profiling in next test cycle.

F-001.finding: T-US01_Overall_Iteration P90 latency 4046 ms vs 500 ms SLA target (+709% deviation) with 100% error rate
F-001.observation: The overall iteration for User Story 01 (Catalog Browse) exhibited a P90 response time of 4046 ms against a 500 ms SLA, and every one of its 226 iterations failed.
F-001.interpretation: This transaction is the single largest contributor to SLA breach and error rate, indicating a fundamental failure in the catalog browse flow under load.
F-001.likely_cause: CPU saturation (91.4% peak) causing request queueing and timeouts, compounded by inefficient catalog data retrieval.
F-001.impact: Complete failure of the primary browsing workflow; users cannot view products.
F-001.recommendation: Immediately investigate catalog launch failures; scale compute resources and optimize catalog queries.
F-001.validation: Re-run test after fix; verify T-US01_Overall_Iteration P90 < 500 ms and error rate < 1%.

F-002.finding: TC01_US01_Launch_Catalog P90 2662 ms vs 500 ms SLA (+432%) with 100% error rate
F-002.observation: The Launch Catalog transaction recorded a P90 of 2662 ms and failed on all 228 attempts.
F-002.interpretation: The entry point to the catalog is completely broken under load, likely due to database connection exhaustion or thread pool saturation.
F-002.likely_cause: Application thread pool exhaustion or database connection pool depletion under CPU saturation.
F-002.impact: Blocks all downstream catalog interactions; direct revenue impact.
F-002.recommendation: Analyze server logs for 5xx root cause; increase thread/connection pool limits; optimize catalog query.
F-002.validation: Confirm zero 5xx errors and P90 < 500 ms in next test.

F-003.finding: Server CPU saturation at 91.4% peak (avg 60.7%) correlating with latency spikes and 5xx errors
F-003.observation: Azure App Service CPU peaked at 91.4% during the test, coinciding with the highest response times and the 168 HTTP 5xx errors.
F-003.interpretation: The compute instance is undersized for the applied load; CPU contention causes request queuing, GC pressure, and thread starvation.
F-003.likely_cause: Insufficient vCPU allocation for the workload; no auto-scaling configured.
F-003.impact: All transactions suffer elevated latency; error rate exceeds SLA by 5.7x.
F-003.recommendation: Scale up App Service plan to higher vCPU tier; enable auto-scaling on CPU > 70%.
F-003.validation: Post-scale test should show CPU peak < 70% and P90 within SLA for all transactions.

F-004.finding: TC02_US04_Navigate_To_Signon_Page P90 578 ms vs 50 ms SLA (+1056% deviation)
F-004.observation: The Signon page navigation transaction exceeded its strict 50 ms SLA by over 10x, with a P90 of 578 ms.
F-004.interpretation: Even lightweight page loads are severely impacted by CPU saturation, indicating systemic resource contention rather than isolated heavy transactions.
F-004.likely_cause: CPU saturation delaying all request processing; possible lock contention in session initialization.
F-004.impact: Signon flow fails SLA dramatically; affects user authentication entry point.
F-004.recommendation: Address CPU saturation first; then profile signon page for unnecessary synchronous work.
F-004.validation: P90 < 50 ms after CPU headroom restored.

F-005.finding: Overall error rate 5.72% (622 errors) vs 1% SLA target; 168 server-side 5xx errors
F-005.observation: The test-wide error rate of 5.72% far exceeds the 1% threshold, driven by three transactions with 100% failure rates and 168 HTTP 5xx responses from the server.
F-005.interpretation: Application instability under load; errors are not transient but systematic for specific transactions.
F-005.likely_cause: Unhandled exceptions due to resource exhaustion (CPU, threads, DB connections).
F-005.impact: Failed user journeys; potential data inconsistency; SLA breach.
F-005.recommendation: Enable detailed error logging; implement circuit breakers; fix root cause of 5xx on catalog launch.
F-005.validation: Error rate < 1% and zero 5xx in subsequent test.

F-006.finding: Extreme tail latency: P99 4489 ms, max 20709 ms (8.9x average)
F-006.observation: The 99th percentile response time reached 4489 ms with a maximum of 20709 ms, indicating severe outliers.
F-006.interpretation: Long-tail latencies suggest intermittent GC pauses, thread blocking, or database lock contention exacerbated by CPU saturation.
F-006.likely_cause: GC pauses under memory pressure (89.3% peak) combined with CPU queueing; possible database lock waits.
F-006.impact: Unpredictable user experience; timeouts for sensitive operations.
F-006.recommendation: Capture GC logs and thread dumps during load; tune JVM heap and GC algorithm; review database locking.
F-006.validation: P99 < 2000 ms and max < 5000 ms in next test.

capacity_planning.saturation_point: CPU saturation observed at ~182 req/s with 91.4% CPU utilization
capacity_planning.safe_concurrency: Approximately 145 req/s (80% of current throughput) before CPU saturation
capacity_planning.analysis: Concurrency (virtual users) was not directly measured. Using Little's Law (concurrency = throughput × response time), average concurrency ≈ 182 req/s × 0.592 s ≈ 108 users. However, without controlled concurrency ramps, the true saturation point cannot be reliably determined. The test shows CPU saturation at the current throughput, indicating the system is already beyond safe capacity. A proper capacity test with incremental user loads and steady-state measurements is required.

root_cause_assessment.finding: CPU saturation on Azure App Service is the primary bottleneck causing queueing, elevated latency, and 5xx errors.
root_cause_assessment.evidence: CPU peaked at 91.4% (avg 60.7%); 168 HTTP 5xx errors; P99 latency 4489 ms; 28/29 transactions breached P90 SLA; error rate 5.72%.
root_cause_assessment.likely_cause: Insufficient vCPU allocation for the workload; no auto-scaling; inefficient code paths in catalog and signon transactions amplify CPU demand.
root_cause_assessment.recommended_investigation: Profile CPU usage per transaction (e.g., via Application Insights or profiler); capture thread dumps at peak load; analyze database query execution plans for catalog launch; enable auto-scaling and re-test.

ai_insights.bottleneck_analysis: The dominant time consumers are the Catalog Launch (TC01_US01_Launch_Catalog, P90 2662 ms) and Signon Navigation (TC02_US04_Navigate_To_Signon_Page, P90 578 ms vs 50 ms SLA). These transactions, along with the overall iteration controllers, account for the highest response times and error rates. CPU saturation (91.4% peak) forces all requests into queueing, inflating latency across the board. The 100% error rate on catalog launch suggests thread pool or database connection pool exhaustion. Database-tier metrics are absent, but the correlation of high CPU with catalog failures points to either application-level lock contention or expensive queries running on a CPU-starved instance. Memory pressure (89.3% peak) may contribute to GC pauses, evidenced by the extreme max latency of 20.7 seconds.
ai_insights.tail_latency_analysis: Tail latency is severe: P95 1533 ms, P99 4489 ms, max 20709 ms. The P99 is 7.6x the average (592 ms), indicating high variability. Outliers likely stem from GC stop-the-world events (memory at 89.3% peak), thread starvation due to CPU saturation, and possible database lock contention. The 100% error transactions (catalog launch) may have timed out after long waits, contributing to the max values. Without GC logs and thread dumps, the exact cause of the 20-second outliers cannot be pinpointed, but the combination of high CPU and high memory pressure makes GC a prime suspect.
ai_insights.infra_analysis: The Azure App Service shows clear CPU saturation: average 60.7%, peak 91.4%. This leaves no headroom for traffic spikes. Memory utilization averages 69.3% with a peak of 89.3%, approaching the threshold where GC frequency increases. Network I/O (43 MB/min in, 27 MB/min out) and disk IOPS (21.9M reads, 9.0M writes over 60s) are moderate and not indicative of bottlenecks. The 168 HTTP 5xx errors confirm the application runtime is failing under resource pressure. The current instance size is inadequate for the applied load; vertical scaling (more vCPU) or horizontal scaling (auto-scale) is required.
ai_insights.correlation_insights: Client-side latency spikes directly correlate with server CPU peaks. The three transactions with 100% error rates (TC01_US01_Launch_Catalog, Transaction Controller_T2, HTTP_US01_Launch_Catalog_Err500) all involve catalog initialization, which likely performs database queries. Under CPU saturation, these queries experience queueing delays, leading to timeouts and 5xx errors. The signon page navigation (TC02_US04_Navigate_To_Signon_Page) exceeds its 50 ms SLA by 1056%, showing even lightweight requests suffer from systemic CPU contention. The 5.72% overall error rate is almost entirely driven by these catalog-related failures; other user stories (US02, US03, US04) have 0% errors but still breach response time SLAs due to the shared resource saturation.

recommendations.title: Scale up Azure App Service and enable auto-scaling
recommendations.why: CPU peaked at 91.4% causing request queueing, 5xx errors, and SLA breaches across 28 transactions.
action: Upgrade to a higher vCPU tier (e.g., P2v3 or P3v3) to provide immediate headroom.
Configure auto-scale rules: scale out when CPU > 70% for 5 minutes, scale in when CPU < 30%.
recommendations.expected_impact: Eliminate CPU saturation; reduce average response time by 50%+; bring error rate below 1%.
recommendations.validation: Re-run load test; verify CPU peak < 70%, P90 < SLA targets for all transactions, error rate < 1%.

recommendations.title: Optimize catalog launch and signon page queries
recommendations.why: TC01_US01_Launch_Catalog P90 2662 ms (+432% over SLA) and TC02_US04_Navigate_To_Signon_Page P90 578 ms (+1056% over SLA) are the worst latency offenders.
action: Profile database queries for catalog launch and signon using Query Performance Insight.
Add caching for catalog category/product data (e.g., Azure Cache for Redis).
Review and add missing indexes on product and category tables.
Convert synchronous signon page initialization to asynchronous where possible.
recommendations.expected_impact: Reduce catalog launch P90 to < 500 ms; signon navigation P90 to < 50 ms.
recommendations.validation: Measure P90 for TC01_US01_Launch_Catalog and TC02_US04_Navigate_To_Signon_Page in staging after changes.

recommendations.title: Resolve 100% error rate on catalog launch and Transaction Controller_T2
recommendations.why: Three transactions failed on every iteration (228/228, 228/228, 100% error rate), driving overall error rate to 5.72%.
action: Analyze application logs for the 168 HTTP 5xx errors; identify exception types and stack traces.
Check thread pool and database connection pool configurations; increase limits if exhausted.
Implement circuit breaker pattern for catalog service calls to fail fast and preserve resources.
recommendations.expected_impact: Eliminate application errors; achieve < 1% error rate SLA.
recommendations.validation: Next test shows zero 5xx errors and error rate < 1% across all transactions.

recommendations.title: Enable Azure SQL performance monitoring and query store
recommendations.why: No database metrics were captured; catalog transactions are likely database-bound but invisible.
action: Enable Azure SQL Query Performance Insight and Query Store.
Monitor DTU/CPU percentage, wait stats, and long-running queries during load.
Correlate database metrics with transaction latency in next test.
recommendations.expected_impact: Visibility into database bottlenecks; targeted query optimization.
recommendations.validation: Database CPU < 70% and no query waits > 500 ms during load test.

executive_summary.assessment_text:
• Only 3.4% of transactions (1 of 29) met defined SLA targets; 28 transactions breached response time or error rate SLAs.
• Peak throughput of 182 req/s drove server CPU to 91.4% saturation, causing average response times of 592 ms (P99: 4,489 ms) and a 5.72% error rate.
• The Catalog Browse user story (US01) completely failed with 100% error rate on launch and iteration transactions, while other user stories succeeded but with elevated latency.
• Primary bottleneck is CPU saturation on the Azure App Service, amplified by inefficient catalog and signon page processing.
• 168 server-side HTTP 5xx errors confirm application instability under load.
assessment_bullets: SLA compliance at 3.4% (1/29 transactions); 28 transactions breached P90 or error rate targets.
Throughput 182 req/s saturated CPU at 91.4% peak; memory peaked at 89.3%.
Catalog Browse (US01) 100% failure rate (226/226 iterations); Signon navigation 10x SLA breach.
168 HTTP 5xx errors recorded; overall error rate 5.72% vs 1% target.
Tail latency extreme: P99 4,489 ms, max 20,709 ms.
conclusions: System cannot support current load profile; CPU saturation is the root cause of latency and errors.
Catalog browse flow is completely broken (100% errors) and must be fixed before any further performance tuning.
Infrastructure scaling is the highest-impact immediate action; code-level optimizations required for catalog and signon.

priority_recommendations.title: Scale up Azure App Service and enable auto-scaling
priority_recommendations.detail: Upgrade to a higher vCPU tier (e.g., P2v3/P3v3) and configure auto-scale rules (scale out at CPU > 70%). This directly addresses the 91.4% CPU peak causing queueing, 5xx errors, and SLA breaches.
priority_recommendations.business_impact: Restores system stability; eliminates 5xx errors; brings 28/29 transactions closer to SLA targets; protects revenue from failed catalog browsing.

priority_recommendations.title: Fix catalog launch 100% failure rate
priority_recommendations.detail: Analyze server logs for the 168 5xx errors; increase thread/connection pool limits; optimize catalog database queries; add caching for catalog data.
priority_recommendations.business_impact: Recovers the primary product browsing workflow; eliminates 100% failure on US01; directly improves conversion funnel entry point.

priority_recommendations.title: Optimize signon page navigation to meet 50 ms SLA
priority_recommendations.detail: Profile TC02_US04_Navigate_To_Signon_Page (P90 578 ms vs 50 ms target); remove synchronous blocking calls; ensure session initialization is lightweight.
priority_recommendations.business_impact: Ensures authentication entry point meets strict latency SLA; reduces login abandonment.

priority_recommendations.title: Enable database observability and tune queries
priority_recommendations.detail: Activate Azure SQL Query Performance Insight and Query Store; monitor DTU/CPU, wait stats, and long-running queries during load; optimize top consumers.
priority_recommendations.business_impact: Provides visibility into data-tier bottlenecks; enables targeted indexing and query tuning to reduce catalog latency.

observations: The test executed 10,881 total samples across 29 transactions at 182 req/s throughput over 60 seconds.
US01 Catalog Browse accounted for 226 overall iterations but with 100% failure rate; US02, US03, US04 completed successfully with 233, 650, and 646 iterations respectively.
Transaction Controller_T1 and _T2 appear as control transactions with high sample counts (231, 228); T2 shows 100% errors, indicating a systemic failure in the controller logic under load.
recommendations: Prioritize fixing US01 Catalog Browse flow which completely failed; investigate root cause of 100% errors on Launch Catalog and Transaction Controller_T2.
Consider pacing adjustments or think-time insertion to reduce concurrency pressure on catalog browsing during peak load.

observations: 28 of 29 transactions breached P90 SLA targets; only one transaction met SLA (3.4% compliance).
Worst offenders: TC02_US04_Navigate_To_Signon_Page P90 578 ms vs 50 ms target (+1056%), T-US01_Overall_Iteration P90 4046 ms vs 500 ms (+709%), TC01_US01_Launch_Catalog P90 2662 ms vs 500 ms (+432%).
Tail latency extreme: P99 4489 ms, max 20709 ms, indicating severe outliers under CPU saturation.
recommendations: Focus optimization on catalog launch and signon navigation paths which exceed SLA by 400-1000%.
Implement caching for catalog data and optimize signon page rendering to reduce CPU demand per request.

observations: Overall error rate 5.72% exceeds 1% SLA target by 5.7x.
Three transactions exhibited 100% error rate: TC01_US01_Launch_Catalog (228/228), Transaction Controller_T2 (228/228), HTTP_US01_Launch_Catalog_Err500 (100%).
168 HTTP 5xx errors recorded server-side, confirming application-level failures correlated with CPU peaks.
recommendations: Analyze server logs for the 5xx errors on catalog launch; likely due to thread exhaustion or database connection pool depletion under CPU saturation.
Implement circuit breaker and retry logic for catalog service calls to improve resilience.

observations: CPU utilization averaged 60.7% but peaked at 91.4%, indicating saturation during peak load; no headroom for traffic spikes.
Memory utilization averaged 69.3% peaking at 89.3%, approaching limits but not saturated; potential GC pressure contributor to tail latency.
Azure App Service returned 168 5xx errors during test, correlating with CPU peaks.
recommendations: Scale up App Service plan to higher vCPU tier or enable horizontal auto-scaling triggered at 70% CPU.
Monitor memory trends; consider increasing memory allocation if GC pressure suspected after scaling CPU.
